policy.holdout_split: Assigned by template family before any read or tuning used a page (Task 7b, 2026-10-29). The rule was written before the first fetch: split groups are template families, joined when a page in one is a copy of the same vacancy as a page in another; within each source class groups are numbered by their lowest slot, and groups 2, 5, 8, ... are holdout. One clause was added when the splits were assigned, after the captures: a family keeps the split it first got in every class. It changed two pages. C04's family (reed-job-details) already had the job class's development split, so it was not numbered again among the course groups; that made C07 (ncs-find-a-course) development rather than holdout, and C08 (uom-undergraduate-course) holdout rather than development. Never moved after the accuracy read or any tuning uses a page (OI-09).
policy.labels: A slot's labels are the England option pack's claims for its page (labels.claims): each a value with its unit or currency, its span (character offsets into the text whose SHA-256 is recorded, or a JSON pointer into an API response) and the exact excerpt there, with the labeller's note. For a page kept as hash and excerpts only, the offsets were located in the capture itself (tools.corpus --locate). label_review records session 2's review (H-07): how many of the page's records it accepted; each record's decision is in the option pack. A correction session 2 made is a new claim whose note names its question.
